content: The test image shows a tomato leaf with large, dark brown necrotic lesions concentrated at the leaf tip and margins. The tissue is clearly dead, with dark brown coloration spreading from the tip. The healthy tissue remains dark green. This pattern of large marginal/tip necrosis is most consistent with **Late Blight**.

The reference image is microscopic (sporangia), so I'll rely on symptom knowledge. The test image shows:
- Large, irregular dark brown necrotic lesions at the leaf tip and margins
- Abrupt boundary between dead and healthy green tissue
- No concentric rings (not Early Blight), no small spots (not Septoria), no mosaic pattern (not virus), no powdery coating

Large irregular marginal/tip necrosis on tomato is the hallmark of **Late Blight** (*Phytophthora infestans*), which starts at leaf edges and creates dark brown water-soaked then desiccated lesions.
